mode: Native PostgreSQL effects for permanent ordinary tables and their columns, in case-sensitive resolved schemas. Use stock catalog naming rules, UTF-8 and the native transaction policy.

RenameTable.role: A name change for one persistent ordinary table in its own resolved schema.
RenameTable.structure: An absolute TableName, an exact destination Identifier, the missing-target policy and the native release.
RenameTable.conditions: A known target is a persistent base-table identity. A complete analysis catalog can establish an optional absence for a known explicit schema. A required same-name change is intrinsically invalid. An optional same-name change preserves the missing-owner and collision effects; conflicts with an independently existing destination are native state-dependent failures.
RenameTable.meaning: Replace only the relation name. Its identity, descendants, stored rows, dependent views and column positions survive. An optional absent target is skipped. PostgreSQL's parsed ONLY flag has no effect on a table name change.
RenameTable.sql: Emit ALTER TABLE with its optional IF EXISTS, absolute old name and ordinary RENAME TO with the exact new name.

RenameColumn.role: A change to one user-defined named column in a persistent ordinary table, with the native descendant policy.
RenameColumn.structure: An absolute TableName, old and new user-column identifiers, descendant mode, missing-target policy and native release.
RenameColumn.conditions: The old column of a known target must resolve to one declared column, and the new name must avoid system columns and known duplicates. Optional known absence follows the table identity rule. A required missing target, missing old column and incompatible child metadata are classified at the analysis or evaluation boundary that has the facts. An optional same-name change succeeds for a known absent owner and observes the exact native failure if the owner later exists.
RenameColumn.meaning: Rename the exact attribute and apply native inheritance propagation or ONLY rejection. Keep ordinals, storage, dependent view field names and column values. The new name is local to the relation.
RenameColumn.sql: Emit exact absolute table and qualified descendant mode, then RENAME COLUMN with both identifiers.

structure: Separate named table and column roles fix the operated object and required names without retaining a catalog description.
conditions: Use permanent ordinary targets with exact names. Forward native IF EXISTS and ONLY where they influence observable effects. Check complete analysis facts before publishing a known relation or optional absolute absence.
meaning: Native ALTER updates the catalog in place, keeps data and references, follows the recorded inheritance rule and participates in rollback.
sql: Quote every identifier at its semantic position.
observations: Exact native relation kind, absolute name, stable object identity, ordered column names and native type IDs
Retained own rows, inherited rows and dependent view result names and values
Known optional absence, conflicting destination, and ONLY rejection with descendants compared as distinct state effects
Same-named cross-schema decoy and exact transaction state and rollback

finite.completeness: Independently recover each axis from the observed complete value and native fixture before evaluating it.

analysis: A table rename with ONLY has the same native effect
An inherited rename without ONLY follows the descendants
An optional explicit absent column owner
An optional explicit absent table renamed to itself
An optional explicit absent column renamed to itself
negative: Direct identical table target and destination without IF EXISTS
Direct identical column identifiers without IF EXISTS
Unqualified optional absent target without an exact schema

exploration.requiredForms: Vary table and column roles, distinct name spellings, absolute identities, inheritance, collisions, absence, descendant policies and both protected fixture witnesses.

faults: Redirect the absolute relation to a decoy
Drop ONLY from a column rename
Admit an inherently invalid same-name rename

evidence.P01: Fix the absolute target, operation and both name roles.
evidence.P02: Check placement, system names, direct distinctness and static relation and column lookup.
evidence.P03: Retain value identifiers and explicit native choices.
evidence.P04: Compose column and relation effects from a resolved identity and native propagation policy.
evidence.P05: Require final immutable types and the shared checked name snapshot.
evidence.P06: Compare exact dependent effects of emitted fully quoted SQL against native behavior.
evidence.Q01: Audit the shape of each constructor and rejection boundary.
evidence.Q02: Require every fixed identity and independently specified analyzed request.
evidence.Q03: Evaluate catalog and live data effects independently, including propagation and transaction state.
evidence.Q04: Compare native resulting metadata, data, exact failures and rollback.
evidence.Q05: Tie observers, replay and both installed Composer layouts to the actual loaded PHP.

open: Partition-specific cases, temporary targets, foreign tables and object or constraint renames
Authorization checks outside the disposable ordinary native fixture
NOTICE delivery other than the required no-op effect
trust: Same interpretation of the absolute relation and column names
Native PostgreSQL and isolated typed catalog observer
Fixed independently selected verifier and exact distributed PHP

amends.change: A required same-name request always fails. An optional same-name request can succeed when the owner is absent. Add observed admission for both optional placements and keep the required negatives.
